feedback.problem: Consider the curve $x+\operatorname{ln}⁡y=4.$ Given that $x=x(t),$   $y=y(t),$  and that $\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}=-1$ on the curve at the point where $x=4,$ find the value of $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}$ at that point.
feedback.worked_solution:
Differentiating the given relation with respect to $t$ using implicit differentiation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x+\operatorname{ln}⁡y & =4 \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(x+\operatorname{ln}⁡y) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(x)+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{ln}⁡y) & =0 \\ \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(x)+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}(\operatorname{ln}⁡y) & =0 \\ \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\cdot 1+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\cdot \frac{1}{y} & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we substitute the given information $\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}=-1$ and $x=4.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}-1+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\cdot \frac{1}{y} & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

We also want to substitute for $y,$ but we are not given this value. However, we can find it by substituting $x=4$ into the equation of the curve.

At the point where $x=4,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}x+\operatorname{ln}⁡y & =4 \\ 4+\operatorname{ln}⁡y & =4 \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡y & =0 \\ y & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting $y=1,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}-1+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\cdot 1 & =0 \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =1.\end{aligned}
$$
